original_question: Given a group Gamma, for which integers k >= 1 and n >= 3 is Gamma the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope or maniplex of rank n?
target_in_paper: The algebraic open-problem theme on how to build k-orbit abstract polytopes/maniplexes from groups: namely, for a fixed symmetry type graph (hence a fixed class of k-orbit objects), characterize the groups that arise as full automorphism groups via a coset-geometry construction, and determine the extra intersection conditions needed in the polytopal case.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main algebraic ingredients: a group Γ, the number k of flag-orbits, the rank n, and the realization problem for automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes/maniplexes. It also correctly restricts attention to rank n >= 3, which is the range emphasized in the later characterization results connected to this problem.
missing_details: The paper’s intent is not a coarse classification only by the pair (k,n); it is finer and depends on the symmetry type graph (the quotient of the flag graph by the automorphism group), i.e. on the specific class of k-orbit polytopes/maniplexes.
The objects are abstract n-polytopes and n-maniplexes; your draft does not say 'abstract' and so is slightly underspecified relative to the paper’s setting.
A 'k-orbit' object means one with exactly k flag-orbits under the action of its full automorphism group; this should be stated explicitly.
The paper frames the problem as a group-theoretic/coset-geometric characterization, not merely as an existence question asking for which integers k and n realization is possible.
For k >= 3, the generating set describing the automorphism group depends on a choice of base flag (root) and a spanning tree of the symmetry type graph; your draft omits this rooted dependence.

The maniplex and polytope cases are not interchangeable: the paper explicitly separates the problem of constructing a k-orbit maniplex from a group from the extra problem of identifying the intersection conditions that force the construction to be polytopal.
The relevant group is the full automorphism group of the object, not just some subgroup acting with k flag-orbits.
The intended question is class-by-class (fixed symmetry type graph / fixed rooted combinatorial data), not globally for all k-orbit types having the same number k of flag-orbits.
Your draft does not mention the coset-geometry reconstruction viewpoint, which is central to the paper’s algebraic formulation.
The paper’s discussion is about a correspondence between k-orbit objects of a given type and groups with distinguished generators; your draft suppresses the generator data entirely.
refined_question: Fix n >= 3 and a rank-n symmetry type graph T with k vertices, so that k is the number of flag-orbits. Which groups Γ occur as the full automorphism groups of abstract n-polytopes, respectively n-maniplexes, having symmetry type graph T? More precisely, can one characterize such Γ by means of a distinguished generating set adapted to a chosen root flag and spanning tree of T, so that the object can be reconstructed as a coset geometry, and determine the additional intersection conditions that are necessary and sufficient for the reconstruction to be an abstract polytope rather than merely a maniplex?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the paper’s algebraic realization problem, but it is broader than the paper’s actual formulation. The paper first treats k-orbit polytopes through symmetry type graphs and discusses how the automorphism group can be generated once a base flag/root is chosen. It then asks how to 'do the same thing' for k-orbit polytopes that is already known for regular and chiral polytopes: namely, how to obtain a correspondence between a particular class of k-orbit objects and an appropriate class of groups. In the authors’ own summary of this direction, the two key tasks are (1) constructing a k-orbit polytope or maniplex from a group with a suitable generating set via coset geometry, and (2) determining which intersection conditions force the resulting object to be polytopal rather than only a maniplex. So the paper-faithful sharpening must fix the symmetry type graph/class and include the generator/intersection-condition data, rather than asking only for which pairs (k,n) a bare group-realization statement holds. This reading is also confirmed by the later paper that explicitly states the solved problem as a characterization of automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes with a given symmetry type graph.
